s: Distributes incoming traffic across backend instances using health checks and algorithms to maximize throughput and availability.
w: Operates at L4 (TCP) or L7 (HTTP) routing requests to healthy upstream targets. Health checks (TCP connect, HTTP 200, gRPC health protocol) continuously probe backends; unhealthy targets are removed from rotation. Algorithms include round-robin, least-connections, and consistent-hashing. Session affinity is optional but discouraged for stateless designs. Cross-zone balancing prevents hotspotting a single AZ.
use: Horizontal scaling of any stateless service tier
Health-check-driven automatic failover removing dead instances from rotation
SSL/TLS termination offloading crypto from application servers
Path-based or host-based routing to different backend pools
avoid: Global anycast steering (that is global_load_balancer's job)

size.rps_per_instance: ~100k L4 rps or ~50k L7 rps depending on payload

pat.d: Envoy sidecar per pod acts as local load balancer with mesh features.

pits: Health-check flapping removing healthy instances during GC pauses - use generous thresholds
Connection draining too fast during scale-in dropping in-flight requests - tune deregistration delay
Sticky sessions causing uneven load - prefer stateless design over affinity
tips: L4 vs L7 tradeoff: L4 is faster (no payload inspection) but L7 enables path routing and compression
Pair with autoscaling_group: LB health checks drive scaling signals
